cues.text: Even the best can lose
In 2003, Gianluigi Buffon was one of the best goalkeepers in the world.
That year he became the only goalkeeper ever to win UEFA’s award for the best club player.
His team, Juventus, reached the Champions League final against Milan.
Flip the scoreboard.
The final ended in a penalty shoot-out, and Juventus lost.
The next season was hard too, because Juventus did not play well.
Buffon later wrote that after this defeat he began to feel very low.
You can try your very best and still lose. A loss does not change who you are.
A heavy grey cloud
Between December 2003 and June 2004, Buffon had depression.
Depression is an illness of the mind.
It can make someone feel sad, tired or empty for a long time, even when everything looks fine from the outside.
Lift the smiling flap.
Years later, Buffon said he also had panic attacks in his early years at Juventus, and once he even missed a game because of them.
The fans saw a superstar in goal.
Inside, he was struggling.
Anyone can feel low, even a hero. How you feel inside really matters.
Someone to talk to
Buffon did not keep it all inside.
Between December 2003 and June 2004, he went regularly to see a psychologist.
A psychologist is a person trained to help us understand our feelings, mostly by listening and talking.
Knock three times on the door.
Week after week, Buffon kept going back to talk.
It took time and patience.
With that help, step by step, he began to feel more like himself again.
Asking for help is strong, not weak. Tell a grown-up you trust how you feel.
The sun comes back
By the summer of 2004, before the European Championship, Buffon had overcome his depression.
He played in every one of Italy’s matches at Euro 2004.
Pull the sun up over the hills.
Two years later, at the 2006 World Cup, Buffon let in only two goals in seven matches, and kept five clean sheets.
Italy won the World Cup, and he was named the best goalkeeper of the tournament.
The grey cloud had not lasted for ever.
Hard feelings can pass. With help and time, things can get better.
Staying with his team
In 2006, soon after the World Cup, Juventus were punished because of a scandal called Calciopoli.
The club was sent down to Serie B, the second division of Italian football.
It was a big fall for a famous team.
Raise the flag back up the ladder.
Buffon decided to stay with Juventus.
He played 37 matches in Serie B, and Juventus won the title and went straight back up to Serie A.
When his team needed him, he was there.
Sticking with your team when times are hard is a kind of courage.
Brave enough to tell
In 2008, Buffon wrote a book about his life, called Numero 1.
In it, he told everyone about his depression.
In 2013 and again in 2019, he spoke about it openly in interviews.
Open the book.
Buffon kept playing until he was 45 years old.
In 2024 he wrote a second book.
Its title means: fall, get back up again, fall, get back up again.
When a hero speaks up, other people can feel less alone.
Talking about feelings is brave. It helps you, and it can help others too.
